Usage

Split the region bbox into an NxN grid; keep cells overlapping the region.

Divides the region's circumscribed axis-parallel rectangle evenly into an N x N grid and returns a mask in which every cell that overlaps the region by even 1 pixel is painted entirely with 1.0. N = 2 + int(a*4): a=0 → 2, a=1 → 6 divisions (a is clipped to [0,1]). The cell boundaries are numpy.linspace(top, bottom+1, N+1) converted to integers; if the bbox is smaller than the number of cells, cells of width 0 arise and are skipped. b is unused.

The return value is a float64 0/1 mask of the same shape as the input. All zeros if there is no foreground. The output is "the union of cells covering the region", so it always contains the input region, and nothing outside the bbox is painted. For a convex region filling the bbox completely, every cell qualifies, and whatever a is, the output is the bbox itself. The coarseness of the grid only becomes visible in regions with large holes or concavities. Uses:

coarse tiling (choosing windows for local processing) and coarse-graining occupancy patterns. Adjacent cells merge into 1 blob, so it is unsuitable for handling cells separately.
